caveat: 9 pairs and one repository. The pair excerpts are single functions, so they can only ever reach model_corroborated -- there is no sibling to be inconsistent with -- and one leak that remains (vampi-books-get-by-title) is a corpus artifact: VAmPI keeps the vulnerable and fixed branches in the same function, so both sides of the excerpt contain the unguarded query.

degradations.detail: no path records; obligations evaluated within entry-point handlers only

found_before_it_was_recorded: get_by_title was flagged by the engine before it was in the recipe. Its code carries the comment '# Broken Object Level Authorization' and the README lists it, so it was a real finding being scored as a false positive. It is now the recipe's third known vulnerability, and all three are entailed.

oracle.pairs: 14 pair cases carry an access_control expectation with a gold label; 9 build a CPG, and 7 of those are from projects unrelated to VAmPI.
oracle.vampi: VAmPI ships an OpenAPI 3 spec whose per-operation `security: bearerAuth` block declares which endpoints require authorization, and every endpoint that declares it calls token_validator in code. Two independent sources agreeing is the ground truth used here, not a reading of the handlers.

vampi_after.note: both remaining false positives are endpoints the spec declares public. That class is untouched by this task.

vampi_before.note: me, delete_user and get_by_title all DO call an authorization guard; get_all_books, get_all_users and register_user are declared public.

reading: Precision on the repository rises 28.6% -> 50.0% and every known vulnerability is still found. The independent check matters more: on the labelled access-control pairs, leak falls 44.4% -> 11.1% with pair_correct unchanged, and on the seven pairs from projects unrelated to VAmPI leak falls 42.9% -> 0.0% with pair_correct unchanged. Every detection lost was on a pair where the FIXED side was flagged too, which scores nothing; no correct detection was traded away.

known.weakness: SQL injection: the username is interpolated into the query string at line 72 and executed at 73
unauthorized password change: the path username is used instead of the authenticated token subject
broken object level authorization: a book is fetched by title with no ownership constraint and its secret returned

still_open: Both remaining VAmPI false positives (register_user, login_user) are endpoints the OpenAPI spec declares public. The arbiter cannot see that declaration, and the mapper's access_level is not a safe substitute: for decorator-based frameworks 'public' means 'no decorator found', which is the bug itself. Recorded as 2.8.
2.7 dominance witnesses carry no line, so access-control sites still read api_views/users.py:?:update_password.

what_was_wrong.a_guard_discharges_the_obligation_it_is_: The largest one. orm-read requires an identity_constraint or an ownership_check; token_validator is a path_guard. Flattened into one list, authenticating the caller discharged an object-level obligation -- so a handler that authenticates and then looks the record up by a PATH parameter read as fully guarded. The facts state the relation; the spec was throwing it away.
what_was_wrong.a_trailing_segment_is_not_a_match: `query.get` was matched by its last segment, so every `.get(` in the repository was a protected database operation: request.headers.get('Authorization') and request_data.get('username') included. Four of the seven false positives came from this, including three handlers that do authorize.
what_was_wrong.a_word_boundary_needs_a_word: Found while fixing the above. Guard matching wrapped every token in (?<![A-Za-z0-9_]) ... (?![A-Za-z0-9_]). The identity token ['sub'] begins with [ and the character before it in resp['sub'] is p, so the assertion could never hold: every identity token starting with punctuation was unmatchable, and the identity constraint that separates a correct lookup from an IDOR was invisible. The boundary now applies only at ends that are word characters.
what_was_wrong.configuration_is_not_authorization: dominance_specs took every obligation fact. `security_setting` operations are configuration, discharged by a VALUE, which config_specs already claims them for. They made app.run(...) an operation requiring an authorization guard and put thirteen tokens in BOTH the operation and discharger lists -- an obligation that is its own discharge.
what_was_wrong.input_validation_is_not_authorization: `validated_input` dischargers (jsonschema.validate, parse_obj) were pooled with the guards. No operation in the table requires them, and counting them marked handlers with no authorization check at all as guarded.
what_was_wrong.two_functions_can_share_a_name: dominance rows were repository-wide, so the model's unguarded delete_user was attributed to the API handler's region. Rows are now scoped to the region's file, which is also what the rung's own justification says: the evidence is a FILE contradicting itself.
